## Verdicts

### Anchored, clickable overlay: verified working

- **Rendering owner.** ImGui inside the Prepare canvas's own frame, through `GLCanvas3D::set_overlay_renderer`. That hook is an existing fork seam. No web content over the GL canvas, no extra window.
- **Position.** The anchor is the top centre of the target copy's bounding box, projected with the camera every frame. Nothing about position is stored. The test computes the projection separately and compares: equal to within 1.5 px after orbit, zoom, window resize and object move.
- **Clicks.** Real pointer events through the canvas's mouse handler and ImGui's hit test press both buttons, the pager and a list row. ImGui takes the pointer first, so a click on the bubble never reaches selection or the camera.
- **Edges.** The bubble is clamped inside the canvas. When the object is off screen or behind the camera, the bubble docks under the pill and says "out of view" rather than disappearing.
- **Highlight.** Selecting an issue selects its copy through the existing `select_copy` command, by OrcaSlicer's instance ID. With two objects of the same name, the right one is selected.

Not verified: display scaling other than this Mac's 2x, Windows and Linux, dark mode, gizmo dragging while a bubble is open.

### Existing chat submission: verified working, with fork-owned additions

Path traced and exercised: button click → `ShellController::submit_issue` → `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` → message appended to the project document → `message_added` to the page → `begin_reply` → `AgentRequest`.

- The message is an ordinary user message. The real chat page drew it with no page change (`08-asked-chat.png`).
- The structured context travels beside the text and reaches the model as labelled source data. Fields sent: issue id, source, severity, native code, setting key, Orca's message; target scope, object ID, copy ID, object name, plate ID; whether Orca has validated, the evidence generation, sliced and slicing flags; workspace session ID and revision. The whole workspace snapshot already goes with every request.
- The composer draft is left alone. The closed chat pane is opened.
- **Missing before this prototype:** any way for native UI to send a user message, and any place on a message to carry context. Both are fork-owned additions (about 70 lines).

### End to end: verified

Warning appears → object highlights → bubble tracks the object and view → each button submits the right visible message and context → native revalidation updates or removes the bubble. Also verified with object deletion and with several issues at once. 314 checks, 0 failures.

## Source and coverage table

"Re-asked" means the reader calls the same public native function OrcaSlicer calls. "Read" means it reads state OrcaSlicer already stores.

| Native source | Example reproduced | Blocks printing natively? | Where the truth lives | Target identity | Goes stale / clears | Prototype |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Print::validate` error | Two cubes 2 mm apart with "By object" sequence; vase mode with two objects | Yes. Plate marked invalid, Slice disabled | Not stored. Re-asked on the plate's `Print` | Copy ID, object ID, or none plus a setting key | Stale for up to 500 ms after an edit; cleared by Orca's next validation | Verified |
| `Print::validate` warning | The handoff's "is too close to others" (by-layer mode) | No | Not stored. Re-asked | Copy ID of the first offender only | Same | Verified |
| Copy over the plate edge | Cube straddling the edge | Yes | `ModelInstance::print_volume_state`, read | Copy ID | Same | Verified |
| Slicing step warnings | "has floating cantilever" on an overhang | No | `Print` and `PrintObject` step state, with Orca's own `current` flag, read | Object ID | Orca marks it not current when its step is invalidated; removed by the next slice | Verified |
| Slice result | "Found gcode path conflicts between…" | No | `Print::get_conflict_result`, slice result warnings, read | Copy ID or none | Gone when the slice is invalidated | Verified (conflict). G-code processor warnings are read but none was reproduced |
| Slicing failure | "No layers were detected" on a 0.02 mm slab | Yes | **Only in the completion event** | Object ID when the error carries one; this one does not | Stale when the project changes; dropped when a slice starts | Verified |
| Plate checks the canvas runs | Filament, TPU, nozzle and mixture compatibility | Some | Public `PartPlate::check_*` functions, re-askable | Plate-wide | Same as validation | **Not prototyped.** Building block confirmed in code only |
| Post-slice bounds | Toolpath beyond plate or height | Yes | Slice result; the fork's `slice_report` already recomputes one | Plate-wide | With the slice | **Not prototyped** |
| Operation errors | Network and download errors pushed as notifications | n/a | Notification only | n/a | n/a | Verified absent from the list |

The "unfamiliar warning" case needs no special handling: the reader has no explanation for any warning. Every entry is Orca's own text plus identifiers, so an unknown one is carried the same way as a known one.

## Native behaviour that shapes the design

Each of these was observed at runtime or read in code, and each changes what the product can promise.

1. **OrcaSlicer's validation holds one error and one warning at most.** A later check overwrites an earlier warning (`Print.cpp:1261` has a FIXME saying so). Several offending objects become one message with several lines and one target. "Several validation findings on one object" cannot happen natively.
2. **A copy over the plate edge is dropped from validation.** With both overlapping cubes over the edge, Orca reported two placement blockers and no clearance warning.
3. **A slice warning survives a plain move.** Moving the object invalidates the slice result but not the step that produced the warning, so Orca still vouches for it. Changing the setting the step depends on (`enable_support`) makes it not current. Only the next slice removes it.
4. **A move made during a slice does not cancel it.** Orca's log shows `apply result=1` (changed, not invalidated) and the slice finished valid. The reader reports Orca's verdict; it does not second-guess it.
5. **Popups are not a list of issues.** Closing a popup removes it while the issue stays true (`issues-07-popup-dismissed.png`). Orca merges slicing warnings that share a message ID into one popup across objects. Targets are captured inside callbacks and cannot be read. Popups are not retired at all while the window is inactive (the count grew from 3 to 10 in one run).
6. **Orca applies an edit to the print on a 500 ms timer.** Until then the print describes the old project. `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is public and tells the reader exactly this. It is what makes "checking" distinguishable from "no issues".
7. **Validation exists only for the active plate.** Other plates are unknown until visited.
8. **The warning's `type` field is uninitialised in some producers** (`StringObjectException warningtemp;` in `Print.cpp`). The reader reports a type only when it is one Orca defines, and never uses it for identity.
9. **Validation costs 0.2 to 0.9 ms** on these fixtures, so asking a second time is cheap here. Not measured on a large plate.

## Lifecycle results

All from `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2/harness-run.log`.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Creation | Issue appears after Orca's own validation, with copy ID |
| Repeated updates | Same issue ID after each revalidation; no duplicates |
| Popup dismissed | Issue stays |
| Edit, before Orca revalidates | List marked stale, pill says "Checking…", buttons off, a forced submit returns `unchecked` |
| Fix, then revalidation | Issue and bubble removed. No "No print issues" shown before the check |
| Undo / redo | Undo brings back the same issue ID on the same copy; redo clears it |
| Object deleted with its bubble open | Its issues go at once, before revalidation; bubble closes; submit returns `expired` |
| Plate switch | List follows the active plate and returns on switching back |
| Project replaced | New session, empty list; an old issue ID cannot be submitted |
| Slice warning, remedy applied, not yet resliced | Shown stale; cannot be submitted; removed only by the new slice |
| Slice fails | Reason listed as a blocker; stale after an edit |
| Edit during a slice | Reader matches Orca's final verdict; no false failure |
| Duplicate object names | Correct copy selected by ID |
| Several issues | Three issues on two objects; one bubble pages through both findings on one object; the list shows all |
| Plate-wide issue | Docked bubble labelled "Whole plate"; no object invented |
| Chat pane closed | Opened on submit |
| Reply running | Buttons off; a forced press sends nothing; the host itself queues a message that arrives mid-reply |
| Agent unavailable | Status keeps working; the question is kept and the reply fails visibly with `agent_unavailable` |
| Same button pressed twice, nothing changed | One message |

Regression: the existing shell scenario passes with the prototype (526 checks), and `agent_bridge_tests` passes (4,691 assertions).

## Intent and permissions

- **Ask AI** sends "Explain this issue and my options." with `intent: explain`. For that turn the request names only the tools whose registry class is read-only (13 today). `OpenAIResponsesAgent` uses that list both to advertise tools and to refuse a call to any other (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:298`). So the limit is enforced by the app, not by wording.
- **Resolve with AI** sends "Help fix this issue." with `intent: resolve` and the ordinary tool set. It adds no tool and removes no check.
- A follow-up typed by the person is a normal turn with normal tools.

Gaps: the limit is applied by the provider adapter, not by `AgentHost` itself, so another adapter would have to honour it too. A host-level refusal is a small hardening step. I did not run a live model, so how well the model uses the context, and whether its words stay within "explain", is unverified. That needs an API key and sends project data to the provider, which I did not do without being asked.

Fork base `3ffb9585d2`, upstream `b3490a1cdc` (local `upstream/main`, not re-fetched).

| Option | Upstream lines | Upstream sites | Upstream changes at those sites since the fork base / in 2 years | Meets the requirements? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Read native state and re-ask native checks (prototype)** | 0 | 0 | n/a | Yes, as tested |
| 1b. Same, declaring the event in `Plater.hpp` | 2 | 2 | 0 / 0 on those lines | Yes. Measured: adds one conflict block against current upstream, resolved by keeping both |

Option 3's numbers are a measurement of the first run's uncommitted diff, not a review of it.

What option 1 depends on, and how it fails if upstream changes it:

- `Print::validate`'s signature and `PartPlate::fff_print()`. Compile error.
- `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` staying a non-static definition in `Plater.cpp`. Compile or link error.
- `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()`. Compile error. Unchanged upstream for at least two years.
- `get_object_clashed_text()`, declared in no header. Link error.
- The meaning of the 500 ms timer. **Silent** if upstream replaces the timer with something else: the reader would call unchecked state checked. The lifecycle test "no all-clear before revalidation" is the guard.
- Any step upstream adds before or after its own validation call. **Silent**, text-only drift between the popup and the bubble.

With the final prototype (commit object `61c2352356`, on no branch) the conflict list is identical. None of the 17 changed files exists in upstream.

## Proposed behaviour

Required:

- One compact status that says one of three things: checking, no issues, or N issues with the number that block. Never "no issues" while Orca has not validated.
- A list of every issue, opened from the status.
- One bubble at a time, for the selected issue, anchored to its object. All findings on that object share the bubble through a pager.
- A docked bubble for plate-wide issues and for objects out of view.
- Both buttons off while Orca has not validated the latest edit and while a reply is running.
- Context resolved at the click. Expired and unchecked issues are not sent.
- Orca's words shown unchanged.

Optional polish: an edge arrow toward an off-screen object, placing the bubble below the object when there is no room above, plain-language rewrites of Orca's text, a context chip on the chat message instead of the quoted text.

The prototype's pill sits on the canvas. The product home for the compact status is the header's status row, which already has the button and menu pieces. That is ordinary UI work, not a feasibility question, and I did not build it. In the prototype the open list also overlaps the bubble; that is a layout defect to fix, not a limit.

## Smallest implementation scope

1. Promote the reader, with the two unprototyped sources added.
2. Header status control in place of the canvas pill.
3. The bubble, to the design system. It uses theme colours and button recipes now, but two widths are literals that need tokens, and the text is ImGui's default font.
4. `submit_issue_message` plus a host-level check of the explain-only limit.
5. Turn the 37-step scenario into a kept harness mode.

Acceptance tests: the lifecycle table above, each row as a harness check, plus the two silent-drift guards named under option 1.

## Decisions for Kenneth

1. **Where the compact status lives.** Header (recommended) or canvas.
2. **What the visible chat message contains.** The prototype quotes Orca's message under the fixed sentence so the chat reads sensibly later. The alternative is the fixed sentence plus a chip, which needs page work.
3. **Agent unavailable.** The prototype follows existing chat behaviour: the question is kept and the reply fails with a retry. The alternative is disabled buttons with a route to agent setup.
4. **Pressing the same button again with nothing changed.** The prototype treats it as the same question and sends nothing.
5. **Other plates.** Show only the active plate (prototype), or mark the others "not checked".
6. **Whether to run a live-model check.** It needs your API key and sends the test project to the provider.

## Not verified

- Live model behaviour for either button.
- Windows, Linux, dark mode, other display scales.
- The two unprototyped sources in the table.
- Large plates (validation cost, bubble overlap with many objects).
- A slicing failure that names its object. The one reproduced carries no object ID natively.
- A click landing in the same event-loop turn as a committed move. In that turn neither native flag is set yet. Real input cannot reach it, because the click handler is queued behind the move's own event; this is reasoning, not a test.

content.text:
The spike is done: JusPrin can keep OrcaSlicer's current print problems visible and actionable outside the chat, and it needs no change to any OrcaSlicer-owned file. I built a working prototype and ran it through 38 lifecycle steps in the real app (324 checks, 0 failures). I did not run a live model, so how well the model uses the issue context is still unverified.

## What works in the prototype

- **Issue list:** a fork-owned reader asks OrcaSlicer's own checks what is wrong with the active plate and re-asks whenever OrcaSlicer's state may have changed. It contains no rule of its own about what counts as a problem.
- **Bubble:** selecting an issue highlights the right object by ID (even with two objects of the same name) and anchors a bubble beside it. The bubble follows camera orbit, zoom, window resize and object moves, and docks under the status pill for plate-wide issues or objects out of view.
- **Chat:** both buttons post an ordinary visible user message into the existing chat, with structured context (issue, object and copy IDs, plate, session, revision) attached for the model.
- **Ask AI vs Resolve with AI:** an Ask AI turn is offered only the 13 read-only tools, and the app refuses calls to any other. Resolve with AI gets the normal tool set and nothing more.
- **Honesty while unsure:** after an edit the list is marked stale, the status says "Checking…", and both buttons are off until OrcaSlicer has re-validated. It never shows "no issues" before that.

The existing shell regression scenario and the agent unit tests still pass with the prototype in place.

## Upstream cost

- **Files changed:** 17, none of which exists in upstream.
- **Merge simulation:** the conflict list against current upstream is identical with and without the prototype.
- **Why zero lines is possible:** the only native fact that could not be read directly was why a slice failed. A declaration in a fork-owned header that `Plater.cpp` already includes made that event observable.

## What the fork would own permanently

- The list of native sources the reader covers (six today). A new kind of OrcaSlicer warning stays invisible until someone adds a reader for it; this is the main ongoing cost.
- Two assumptions that would fail silently if upstream changed them; the report names both and the tests that guard them.
- The status, list and bubble UI, the chat entry point, and the tests.

## Not covered

- Live model behaviour for either button.
- Windows, Linux, dark mode and other display scales.
- Two native sources: the filament and nozzle compatibility checks, and toolpath-out-of-bounds after slicing.
- The compact status in the header: the prototype draws it as a pill on the canvas instead.

## Decisions for you

1. Should the compact status live in the header (my recommendation) or on the canvas?
2. Should the visible chat message quote OrcaSlicer's text, as the prototype does, or show a chip (needs chat page work)?
3. With no agent configured, should the buttons send and fail visibly with a retry, as chat does today, or be disabled with a route to setup?
4. Do you want a live-model check? It needs your API key and sends the test project to the provider, so I did not run one unasked.

Two smaller ones (repeat presses, other plates) are in the report.

## Where things are

Everything is uncommitted in the spike's worktree. This session is blocked from writing to the main checkout, so the report is not next to the handoff.

- Report: [investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md](investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md)
- Screenshots and run log: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2/`
- Prototype code: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/`
- Test scenario: [print_issues_spike_scenario.inc](tests/shell/print_issues_spike_scenario.inc)

The worktree's build directory takes about 15 GB and the disk has 17 GB free; say if you want it removed.

The app is running and should now be in front: a window titled JusPrin with two overlapping cubes on the plate. It is the prototype build from the spike's worktree, started with its own throwaway settings folder, so it does not touch your real JusPrin data. I have not looked at the window myself in this launch; the harness reported ready with no failures.

## What to try

1. **Status pill**, top right of the 3D view. It should say "1 print issue". Click it to open the list.
2. **Click the row** in the list. The cube OrcaSlicer named gets selected and the bubble appears above it.
3. **Orbit, zoom, resize the window, drag the cube a little.** The bubble should stay attached. While OrcaSlicer re-checks after a drag (about half a second) the pill says "Checking…" and the buttons grey out.
4. **Close OrcaSlicer's own orange warning popup** (bottom right). The pill and bubble should stay.
5. **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI.** Each posts a message into the chat pane on the right. Close the chat pane first to see it reopen.
6. **Drag the cubes apart.** The bubble and the issue should disappear once OrcaSlicer re-validates. Undo should bring them back.
7. **Drag a cube half off the plate** to get a blocking issue ("Blocks printing").

## Things that will look wrong but are expected

- **The assistant only ever answers "Noted."** This launch uses a stand-in agent, not a real model, so you can see the message and context go through but not a real explanation. Say if you want it relaunched against the live model; that needs your API key from your JusPrin settings.
- **The open list overlaps the bubble.** Known layout defect in the prototype.
- **The status is a pill on the canvas**, not in the header. That is the prototype stand-in.
- **Bubble text uses the canvas's default font**, not the design system's.

Quit it like any app when you are done (Cmd+Q). It is process 92685 if it needs killing.

content.text:
Yes to both. The handoff states them in its opening paragraph and again as requirement 2.

**Opening paragraph:**
> "Investigate the complete interaction: highlight an affected object, anchor a clickable issue bubble beside it, and submit either **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** to the existing chat…"

**Requirement 2, under "What the proposed experience must support":**
> "Selecting an issue highlights its affected object when a reliable native target exists. Anchor an issue bubble beside that object, following camera movement, zoom, and object movement. Plate-wide or untargeted findings need an explicit fallback, not a fabricated object target. Duplicate object names must not select the wrong object."

It also guards the bubble requirement in the hand-back section:
> "Do not replace the anchored-bubble requirement with a status-row-only proposal without explicitly reporting the gap."

How the prototype you have open interprets that, in case it is not what you are seeing:

- **Nothing is highlighted and no bubble shows until you select an issue.** The handoff says "selecting an issue highlights", so on launch you only get the pill. You have to click the pill, then a row in the list.
- **The highlight is OrcaSlicer's ordinary selection.** Selecting an issue selects that object, so it gets the normal selection outline. There is no separate "this object has a problem" colour or marker.
- **The highlight goes away if you click elsewhere.** The bubble stays, because it follows the issue's object, not the selection.

If you expected the offending object to be marked and the bubble to appear on its own as soon as the warning exists, the prototype does not do that. The handoff's wording does not ask for it, but it is a small change if it is what you want.

content.text:
Yes. The handoff says "Anchor an issue bubble **beside** that object", and its feasibility section says to check "viewport boundaries" for exactly this situation. What your screenshot shows is a defect in my prototype, not a gap in the handoff.

**What is going wrong:** the bubble is placed above the object. When the object is near the top of the view there is no room above it, and my code then just pushes the bubble down until it fits inside the canvas, which lands it on top of the object (and on top of the tool strip). My test checked that the bubble stays inside the canvas and points at the right place, but never that it avoids covering the object. I also filed "place the bubble elsewhere when there is no room above" under optional polish in the report. That was wrong; it is part of the requirement.

I'm fixing it now: first a test that reproduces your screenshot and fails, then the placement fix.

The bubble no longer covers the object. I replaced the app you had open with the fixed build, so the window in front of you now is the new one (your previous window was closed and its state is gone; it is back to the two overlapping cubes).

## What changed

- **Placement:** the bubble goes above the object when there is room. Otherwise it takes the object's right, left or underside, whichever fits inside the 3D view.
- **Things it now stays clear of:** the object itself, the status pill, the open issue list, and the tool strip. Your screenshot showed it covering the tool strip too; that is the same fix.
- **No free side at all** (object fills the view): the bubble docks under the pill instead.

## How I checked it

1. Added a test step that puts the object 60 px below the top edge, as in your screenshot. Against the old code it failed on "bubble does not cover its object".
2. After the fix the same step passes, with the bubble placed below the object. The right side was rejected because it would cover the pill, and the left because it would cover the tool strip.
3. The whole scenario still passes: 39 steps, 334 checks, 0 failures.

The picture of the fixed case is `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2/issues-05c-object-near-top.png`.

## Two things I got wrong earlier

- My original test only checked that the bubble stayed inside the canvas and pointed at the right spot, never that it avoided the object. That is why 324 green checks missed this.
- The report listed "place the bubble elsewhere when there is no room above" as optional polish. It is part of the "beside" requirement. The report now says so and records that you found it by hand.

To retry your exact case: drag a cube to the top-left corner of the plate so it hangs over the edge, then pick the issue from the list.

No. I just re-checked after the bubble fix: none of the changed or new files exists in upstream OrcaSlicer, and nothing was touched outside the fork's own folders.

- **Product code:** all under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
- **Test code:** all under `tests/shell/`, which upstream does not have.
- **Merge simulation against current upstream:** the conflict list is identical with and without the prototype. I ran this before the bubble fix; the fix only changed files in the fork's own folder.

Two things come close to upstream without editing it, and they are the dependencies to watch on a rebase:

1. **The slice-failure event.** OrcaSlicer defines it in `Plater.cpp` but declares it in no header. I declared it in a fork-owned header that `Plater.cpp` already includes, which makes it visible to fork code. If upstream renames or moves that event, the build breaks rather than misbehaving.
2. **Calls into public OrcaSlicer functions.** The reader calls `Print::validate` and `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()`. Signature changes would break the build. A change in what the 500 ms update timer means would not; that one is guarded by a test.

I did try a variant earlier that added two lines to upstream's `Plater.hpp`. The merge simulation showed it would create one new conflict, so I dropped it and restored that file to upstream's text.

content.text:
I have not built this, so what follows is a proposal from reading the code, not something tested.

**Recommendation: a per-type "do not draw" filter in OrcaSlicer's notification manager, about 5 added lines in two upstream files.** Every popup is drawn by one loop in `NotificationManager::render_notifications`, called from one place in the canvas. A neutral setter such as `set_hidden_types(...)` plus one `continue` in that loop hides the chosen kinds. Which kinds to hide stays in fork code.

## Why this option

| Option | Upstream lines | What it does | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Skip drawing by type (recommended)** | about 5 added, 0 changed | Popups still exist and follow OrcaSlicer's own push, close and grey-out logic; they are just not drawn | None found yet |
| Close them from fork code after OrcaSlicer pushes them | 0 | Uses the public `close_notification_of_type` | Depends on the fork running between the push and the next frame, so it can flicker. It also changes native state, and OrcaSlicer re-pushes on every re-check |
| Refuse them at insertion, through the fork's existing file-load hook in `push_notification_data` | about 1, at a line the fork already owns | The popup never exists | Changes native state. Not reversible until OrcaSlicer pushes again |
| Skip the whole `render_notifications` call | about 2 | Hides everything | Also hides slicing progress, export finished, downloads, network errors and update notices |

The recommended option is the only one that leaves OrcaSlicer's notification state untouched, which is what makes it safe to turn off again (for example when switching back to the stock presentation).

Upstream activity at the two places it would touch, since the fork base and over two years:
- the drawing loop: 1 and 3 changes;
- the header next to the similar `set_in_preview`: 0 and 0.

## The constraint that matters more than line count

Hide only the popup kinds the issue list already covers; everything else must keep showing. That gives two rules:

1. **Hide by an explicit list, never "all warnings".** A new kind of OrcaSlicer warning that the issue reader does not know about then still appears as a native popup. That also softens the main ongoing cost I named in the report.
2. **Two popup kinds are shared with sources the prototype does not read yet.**
   - "Slicing error" is used for slice failures (covered) and also for toolpath-out-of-bounds and filament compatibility errors (not covered).
   - "Plater error" is used for an object over the plate edge (covered) and for at least one other producer in `Plater.cpp` that I have not traced.

   I can only filter by kind, not by text, so those two kinds cannot be hidden until the reader covers the remaining sources. Hiding them earlier would silently drop real blockers.

What can be hidden safely today: validation errors, validation warnings, slicing step warnings, and the path-conflict warning. I would still confirm each kind's producers before switching it off.

## Decision for you

Do you want me to prototype this? It would mean the first real upstream edit in this spike (about 5 lines). I would also add the two missing sources to the reader first, so the "slicing error" and "plater error" popups can go too. The merge simulation would be rerun afterwards.

content.text:
One correction first: the prototype does not intercept anything. It reads OrcaSlicer's state alongside the popups, which is why you still see both. Hiding the popups is a separate step, and that is where the question of "all or some" comes in.

For print problems, I agree with you: the end state should be that JusPrin shows all of them and the matching popups are hidden. The reasons to leave some popups showing fall into two groups.

## Temporary reasons (go away as the work is finished)

- **Sources the reader does not cover yet.** Filament and nozzle compatibility checks and toolpath-out-of-bounds are not read by the prototype. If their popups were hidden today, real blockers would disappear with nothing replacing them.
- **Popups that carry a native action.** Some have a link that does something specific: "Click here to regroup" for filament grouping, a link that opens the flushing-volume dialog, a wiki link, "Jump to" a setting. Those actions live inside OrcaSlicer callbacks that fork code cannot read. Hiding such a popup removes the action until the bubble offers an equivalent.

## Permanent reasons

- **Most notifications are not print problems.** The same popup system carries about 70 kinds, including slicing progress with its cancel button, export finished with "open folder" and "eject", upload-to-printer progress, download progress, update available, sync conflicts with their own buttons, and tips. The handoff explicitly says not to put these in a print-readiness list.
- **Events are not states.** The issue reader works because a print problem is a current state it can re-ask OrcaSlicer about. "Export finished" or "network error" is a one-time event with nothing to re-ask. Taking those over needs a different mechanism (capturing them as they are pushed), which means more upstream surface and a different JusPrin surface to show them, such as a toast or a chat note.
- **New warning kinds from upstream.** If the rule is "hide everything", a warning upstream adds next year is silently invisible until someone notices and writes a reader for it. If the rule is "hide only the kinds we have taken over", a new kind shows up as a stock popup. That looks inconsistent, but nothing is lost. I would keep this default permanently.
- **Some warnings are not popups at all.** A critical slicing failure opens a modal error box, exporting with warnings opens a "warnings after slicing" dialog, and some setting changes open a confirmation (I hit the vase-mode one in testing). Hiding popups does not touch these; they are separate work if you want them replaced.

## What I would do

1. Finish the reader for the two missing print sources, and give the bubble equivalents for the native action links.
2. Hide every print-problem popup kind at that point, by explicit list.
3. Leave operation notices (progress, export, upload, updates) with OrcaSlicer for now, and decide separately whether JusPrin should own those too.
4. Keep "unknown kinds stay visible" as the standing rule.

content.text:
Here are the parts of the handoff that set the scope, quoted, with what each one led me to do. Some shortcuts were my own judgement rather than the handoff's, and I list those separately so they are not blamed on the document.

## What the handoff said

| Handoff text | How I read it | What it produced in the code |
|---|---|---|
| "This is a feasibility investigation, not authorization to implement a new warning system or automatic remediation." | The deliverable is an answer, not a feature. | Code written to prove each claim once, not to be maintained. |
| "Begin read-only. If code inspection cannot settle feasibility, propose the smallest isolated prototype…" | Any code is a means to settle a question, and should be as small as possible. | The status is a pill on the canvas instead of a header control. Only the active plate is handled. Two native sources were left unread. |
| "Return a short untracked report" containing "the smallest proposed implementation scope, acceptance tests, and decisions requiring user input." | Implementation is a later step that someone scopes from the report. | I listed production work as future scope instead of doing it. |
| "This handoff is temporary: keep it and your investigation report untracked…" | Nothing here is meant to land. | Nothing committed; no docs updated. |
| "A minimal proposed bubble placement… distinguish required behavior from optional polish." | There is a "polish" bucket that can be deferred. | I put "move the bubble when there is no room above" in that bucket. That was a misfiling on my part; you caught it. |
| "Use a bounded set of representative real-app cases." | Coverage by example, not exhaustive. | One fixture per case, one platform, light mode only. |
| "If no patch is produced, explicitly state that patch-level merge risk remains unmeasured." | A patch is optional. | Reinforced that the code itself was secondary to the measurements. |

Your own words pointed the same way: "do this spike" and "prototype pre-approved". The branch name also contains "spike".

## Shortcuts that were my choice, not the handoff's

- **Design system rules skipped.** Two widths are typed as literals with no token, and the text uses the canvas's default font. `design-system.md` says to add the token first; I left a comment instead.
- **User-facing strings are hard-coded English**, not passed through translation.
- **A second copy of message-sending logic.** `submit_issue_message` repeats about half of the existing page-message handler instead of both sharing one path.
- **The "explain only" tool limit sits in the provider adapter**, not in the host, so a different adapter would not enforce it.
- **The bridge protocol description was not updated** for the new `issueContext` field, and the chat page ignores the field.
- **Two reach-arounds into OrcaSlicer:** an undeclared function declared by hand to get one error text, and a listener on every timer the plater owns rather than only the one that matters.
- **No small, fast tests.** Everything is proven through one long real-app scenario kept in an include file. The reader and the bubble layout have no unit tests, unlike the tool strip, whose layout is a separate tested unit.
- **Drawing and layout live in one 400-line function.**
- **Comments say "SPIKE"** in about ten places.

## What this means for making it production ready

The handoff does not need to change for the facts in the report to stand; the native findings and the zero-upstream result hold either way. What changes is the bar for the code. The list above is the gap between the two.

Three items in it depend on decisions you have not made yet: where the compact status lives (header or canvas), what the chat message shows (quoted text or a chip), and whether to hide the native popups (the first upstream edit). Everything else I can start on without an answer.

edit('agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md', '''### Agent WebView

The production Agent interface''', '''### Print issues

What is wrong with the active plate stays on the Prepare canvas whether or not the chat is open: a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**. OrcaSlicer's own notices are not drawn while the shell is installed.

| Piece | Owns |
|---|---|
| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | The list. It asks OrcaSlicer's own checks again and reads the state OrcaSlicer already stores; it holds no rule about what a problem is. An entry exists while its native source reports it, and is marked stale while OrcaSlicer has an edit it has not yet applied to the print. |
| `PrintIssues/PrintIssue.hpp` | The entry: OrcaSlicer's words unchanged, a severity taken from whether OrcaSlicer itself refuses to slice or print, and the object and copy ids OrcaSlicer named. Ids come from the native source's identifiers, never from the message text. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout` | Where the pieces go, as plain geometry with its own tests. The bubble goes above its object, else right, left, or below; it never covers the object, the pill, the open list, or the tool strip, and docks beside the pill when no side is free or the issue has no object. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlay` | Drawing and input, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. Position is recomputed from the camera every frame. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueContext` | The chat message a button sends: the request sentence, OrcaSlicer's words quoted beneath it, and the issue, its target and the freshness of the evidence as data for the model. |
| `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. It shares the page's path, obeys the same refusals, and leaves the composer's draft alone. |

Rules that follow from the above:

- **Never "no issues" before a check.** While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the status says it is checking and both buttons are off.
- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer stops reporting it. Closing a notice, pressing a button, or an agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
- **A press acts on what is true at the press.** The issue is looked up again; one that has cleared or gone stale is not sent.
- **Ask AI may only read.** The turn is offered the read-only tools and `AgentHost` refuses a call to any other, whatever the service asks for. Resolve with AI is an ordinary turn with no extra authority.
- **A new kind of native warning needs a reader.** With OrcaSlicer's notices hidden, a warning the monitor does not read is not shown anywhere. After an upstream update, check `GLCanvas3D::EWarning`, `NotificationType`, and the callers of the notification manager's `push_*` functions for sources the monitor lacks. Known gap: the "flushing volume set to 0" warning, whose check is private to `GLCanvas3D`.
- **Operation notices are not print issues.** Export finished, upload and download progress, update and network notices have no JusPrin surface yet; hiding OrcaSlicer's notices hides them too.

### Agent WebView

The production Agent interface''')

edit('agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md', '''### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners''', '''### Print problems are read back from OrcaSlicer, not recorded as they pass

OrcaSlicer reports print problems through three unrelated producers (print
validation in `Plater`, slicing steps on the background thread, plate checks in
`GLCanvas3D`), and all three end in `NotificationManager`. The notices are a
presentation, not a record: a closed notice is gone while its problem remains,
several objects' warnings are merged into one notice, and the object a notice
is about is captured inside a callback nobody else can read.
`PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` therefore reads the facts where OrcaSlicer
keeps them, and changes no OrcaSlicer function to do it.

- **Validation is asked again.** `Print::validate` is public and `const`, and
  `PartPlate::fff_print()` hands out the plate's print. It costs under a
  millisecond on small plates. It returns one error and one warning at most:
  a later check overwrites an earlier warning, and several offending objects
  become one message with one target. The warning's `type` is left
  uninitialised by some producers, so never use it for identity.
- **The print lags the project by up to 500 ms.** An edit schedules
  OrcaSlicer's update of the print on a timer.
  `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is true until it runs;
  until then nothing read from the print describes the project as it is. This
  is what separates "checking" from "no issues".
- **A copy over the plate's edge is dropped from validation.** It gets a
  placement error instead and no clearance warning.
- **Step warnings carry their own freshness.** `step_state_with_warnings`
  keeps a warning whose step was invalidated, with `current == false`, until
  the step runs again. A plain move invalidates the slice result but not the
  object's steps, so the warning stays current; changing a setting the step
  depends on does not.
- **A move during a slice does not cancel it.** `Print::apply` reports
  "changed", not "invalidated", and the slice finishes valid.
- **Why a slice failed exists only in `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`**, which
  `Plater.cpp` defines and no header declares. `Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp`
  declares it; `Plater.cpp` includes that header ahead of the definition, so
  the event gets external linkage with no OrcaSlicer line changed. The
  completion handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()`.
- **OrcaSlicer validates only the active plate.**
- **The notification manager stops retiring notices while its window is
  inactive**, so a count of notices only grows there.

`NotificationManager::set_render_suppressed` stops the notices being drawn and
nothing else: they are still pushed, timed out and closed, because that
lifecycle runs in `update_notifications`, not in the draw. The shell sets it
on install and puts the previous value back on detach.

### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners''')
EOF
tail -2 build/build14.log | cut -c1-120

content.text:
The print-issues feature is now production-grade code with your three decisions applied, and every test passes. The app window in front of you is the new build. Nothing is committed yet.

## Your three decisions

- **OrcaSlicer's notices are all hidden** while the JusPrin shell is installed. Switching back to the stock presentation shows them again.
- **The status sits in the lower right corner** of the 3D view, where the notices were. Its list opens upward and scrolls if it runs out of room.
- **The chat message quotes OrcaSlicer's text** under the request sentence.

## Upstream footprint: 6 added lines, not 2

You made hiding conditional on about two lines. The real number is 6 added lines and 0 changed, in OrcaSlicer's two notification manager files (header and source): a setter, a getter, a member, a comment, and a two-line early return. Say so if that is over your limit.

The 2-line version I quoted would have guarded the draw call in the canvas file, which upstream changes more often and where the guard would only cover one of the canvases.

The merge simulation shows no new conflict against current upstream. It also caught a mistake in my first placement. Upstream has since added a line at the top of that drawing function, and my early return would have skipped it after a rebase. I moved the return one line down, and the merge is now clean with upstream's line running first.

## What else changed to make it production code

- **Coverage:** with all notices hidden, any warning the issue list does not read is shown nowhere. So the list now also reads OrcaSlicer's filament and nozzle plate checks and its post-slice bounds checks.
- **Ask AI can only read:** the chat host itself now refuses a changing tool on an "explain" turn, whatever the model provider code does.
- **One message path:** typed messages and button messages go through the same code in the chat host.
- **Design system:** the two widths are tokens with guard tests, and all text goes through translation.
- **Tests:** bubble placement and the chat message builder are separate units with fast tests; your "bubble covers the object" case is one of them.
- **Docs:** the architecture guide and the OrcaSlicer integration guide each have a new section.

## Test results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Real-app print-issues scenario, light and dark | 39 steps, 336 checks each, 0 failures |
| Existing shell regression | 527 checks, 0 failures |
| Switch back to stock presentation | notices return, 0 failures |
| Chat host unit tests (5 new) | 4,756 assertions pass |
| Layout and message unit tests (9 new) | pass |
| Token guard tests | pass, apart from one failure the suite already marks as allowed, unrelated to this work |

## What hiding everything costs

- **Operation notices are gone with no replacement:** export finished, upload and download progress, update available, network and sync errors, and the object-size card. Slicing progress and cancel are still in the header.
- **One known print warning is not covered:** "flushing volume set to 0". Its check is private inside OrcaSlicer, so reading it needs another upstream edit.
- **New warning kinds from upstream will be invisible** until someone adds a reader. The architecture guide now says what to check after each upstream update.
- **The new plate and post-slice readers were never triggered at runtime.** The test printer has one nozzle and no TPU, so they are checked by build and code reading only.

## Still open

- Live model behaviour for either button has not been run.
- Windows and Linux are untested.
- Earlier decisions you have not answered: what happens with no agent configured, repeat presses, and other plates.

The report has a new section at the top with all of this: [investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md](investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md). Tell me when you want it committed.

Isn't it true that whenever it's in the shell, this should be true? we don't want them to show in the The G-code viewer mode either. The only reason why we want them to show is when the user switch back to classic mode.
This probably means that we can use some existing flag that check if the shell is on.
Yes, you’re right, and there’s an existing flag that fits: the new member, setter and getter can all go.
The flag to reuse
`GLCanvas3D::legacy_overlays_hidden()` (GLCanvas3D.hpp:887). The shell already sets it on the Prepare canvas at install, and `CanvasPresentationController` already saves and restores the previous value on detach, so switching back to classic mode shows the notices again with no extra code.
`render_notifications` is already handed the canvas as its first argument, so the whole upstream change becomes two added lines in one file:

```
	sort_notifications();
	if (canvas.legacy_overlays_hidden())
		return;
```

That gives:

* Upstream footprint: 2 added lines in `NotificationManager.cpp`, 0 in the header (down from 6 across two files).
* Same position as the current guard, after `sort_notifications()`, so the clean merge against upstream’s new `m_imgui_ready` line should hold. That needs the simulation rerun to confirm; I can’t run it from here.
* Fork-side cleanup: `m_saved_notifications_suppressed` and the two `set_render_suppressed` calls in `ShellController.cpp` (lines 582–583 and 872) go away. The two harness checks switch to reading `legacy_overlays_hidden()`.

It also reads sensibly: that flag’s own comment says it suppresses “the whole legacy canvas-overlay layer” so the fork’s UI owns the canvas, and the notices are one more legacy overlay.
Two things it does not do by itself

* It is per canvas, and only the Prepare canvas has it set. The Preview canvas and the Check print window would still draw OrcaSlicer’s notices. To hide them there too, the shell would have to set the flag on those canvases as well. I have not checked what else that flag hides on a Preview canvas (it also turns on `only_body` at GLCanvas3D.cpp:2059 and skips `_render_overlays`), so that needs a look before doing it. There’s also an argument for leaving them: the print-issue overlay only exists on the Prepare canvas, so in Check print the native notice is the only thing showing a post-slice problem.
* G-code viewer mode is not covered by any “shell is on” flag, because the shell is never installed there (`attach_shell` returns early on `!is_editor()`). Hiding notices in that mode needs something to set the flag outside the shell, and nothing would replace them, since there is no JusPrin overlay in the viewer. I don’t know whether JusPrin ships that mode to users at all.

The flag I would not use
`Plater::is_sidebar_available()` is also false while the shell is installed and is app-wide, which would cover every canvas. But it means something unrelated, and the harness’s `--manual-mcp` mode turns the sidebar back on inside the shell (shell_harness.cpp:846), so notices would reappear there.
Since this is a side chat, the change itself has to be requested in the main conversation: “replace `m_render_suppressed` with a check on `canvas.legacy_overlays_hidden()`”, plus your call on Preview and Check print.
</pasted_content id="dbda">

make this change.

input.title: Close the gaps left by hiding OrcaSlicer's notices
input.tldr: The print-issues work in this session hides every OrcaSlicer notice inside the JusPrin shell, which leaves four known holes: operation notices have no replacement, one print warning is unreadable, future upstream warnings would be invisible, and several new readers were never triggered at runtime. This task investigates each and proposes (not ships) a solution.
input.prompt:
You are picking up four open problems from a feature called "print issues" in JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, OpenGL). Investigate each and write a proposal with evidence. Do not ship fixes without Kenneth's approval; a small isolated prototype to prove a point is fine.

## Where the work is

- Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Production branch: `jusprin-newui`.
- The feature is UNCOMMITTED in the git worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009` (branch `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1`). Another session owns that worktree. Do NOT work in it, build in it, or check anything out there. Read its files freely. If you need to run code, create your own worktree and copy the uncommitted changes into it (`git -C <that worktree> diff` plus the untracked files listed by `git -C <that worktree> status --short`), or wait until Kenneth has committed the feature and branch from that commit. Ask Kenneth which he prefers if it matters.
- Read first: `AGENTS.md`, then in `agent-docs/jusprin/` of that worktree: `architecture.md` (section "Print issues"), `orca-integration-guide.md` (section "Print problems are read back from OrcaSlicer, not recorded as they pass"), and `fork-stewardship.md` (required before touching any OrcaSlicer-owned file: every upstream line changed is re-resolved at every rebase; run the merge simulation it describes and report both endpoint commits).
- Background report with measurements: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md` in that worktree's root (untracked on purpose; never commit it or hide it with ignore rules).

## What the feature does

Inside the JusPrin shell, OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notices (the stack in the lower right corner of the 3D view) are no longer drawn. Instead:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor.{hpp,cpp}` builds a list of current print problems for the active plate by re-asking OrcaSlicer's own public checks and reading state OrcaSlicer already stores. It contains no rule of its own about what is a problem. Sources it reads today: `Print::validate` (one error and one warning at most), a copy straddling the plate edge (`ModelInstance::print_volume_state`), a filament its nozzle cannot reach (via `GLCanvas3D::check_volumes_outside_state`), the plate checks `PartPlate::check_tpu_printable_status`, `check_filament_printable`, `check_mixture_of_pla_and_petg`, `check_compatible_of_nozzle_and_filament`, `check_mixture_filament_compatible`, prime tower outside the plate, slicing step warnings (`step_state_with_warnings`), the slice result (path conflict, G-code processor warnings, toolpath outside the build volume, `gcode_check_result`, `filament_printable_reuslt`), and the reason a slice failed (captured from `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`).
- `PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.{hpp,cpp}` draws a status pill in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas, a list, and a bubble beside the affected object with "Ask AI" and "Resolve with AI". Layout rules are in `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout.{hpp,cpp}`.
- The only upstream edit is two added lines in `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.cpp`, inside `render_notifications`, after `sort_notifications()`: it returns early when `wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden()` is true. That flag is one the shell already sets on install and restores when the person switches back to the stock ("classic") presentation. Only drawing stops: notices are still pushed, timed out and closed, because that lifecycle runs in `NotificationManager::update_notifications`.
- Tests: `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` (run with the shell harness, `--print-issues` or `--print-issues-capture <dir>`; build target `shell_integration_harness`), `tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp`, and the "[print-issues]" cases at the end of `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`.

Kenneth decided to hide ALL native notices. The four problems below are the cost of that decision.

## Problem 1: operation notices are gone with no replacement

The same notification manager also carries notices that are not print problems, and hiding everything hides them too: export finished (with "open folder" and "eject"), upload-to-printer and download progress, update available, network and sync errors (including a sync conflict notice with its own action buttons), tips, and the object-size card. Slicing progress and its cancel action are still available in the JusPrin header. The full list of kinds is the `NotificationType` enum in `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.hpp`.

Deliver: an inventory of every `NotificationType` with who pushes it, whether it is a one-time event or a lasting state, whether it carries an action (a hypertext callback or buttons), and whether JusPrin already shows the same fact somewhere (header, chat, Home). Then a proposal for where each kind that matters should appear in JusPrin and by what mechanism. Note the key difficulty: print problems are states that can be re-asked from OrcaSlicer, but these are events with nothing to re-ask, so they need to be captured as they are pushed. The fork already has one hook at the single insertion point (`report_file_load_message` in `NotificationManager::push_notification_data`, see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/FileLoads.hpp`); evaluate whether that seam can be generalised with little or no extra upstream footprint. The product definition (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`) says which surfaces must remain; the original handoff required keeping operation failures out of the print-readiness list.

## Problem 2: "flushing volume set to 0" is not covered

OrcaSlicer warns "Partial flushing volume set to 0. Multi-color printing may cause color mixing in models." The check is `GLCanvas3D::is_flushing_matrix_error()` in `src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp`, which is private, so the monitor cannot call it and this warning is now shown nowhere. Options to compare with measured upstream cost: make that one function public (a one-word upstream change; measure upstream history at that line), find another public route to the same fact, or read the notice's presence from the notification manager. Do not copy the check's logic into fork code: duplicated logic drifts from upstream silently.

## Problem 3: new warning kinds from upstream will be invisible

A warning OrcaSlicer adds in a future version is drawn nowhere until someone writes a reader for it, and nothing fails to tell us. Propose a guard. Ideas to evaluate, not a prescribed answer: (a) a catch-all reader over the notification manager's current warning- and error-level notices for kinds no specific reader claims, shown as plate-wide issues with OrcaSlicer's raw text (needs a small read accessor on `NotificationManager`, an upstream edit, so measure it; note that with drawing suppressed nobody can dismiss a notice, which removes the main weakness of reading notices); (b) a test that fails when `NotificationType` or `GLCanvas3D::EWarning` gains a value the fork has not classified; (c) a check run after each upstream rebase. Two notification kinds are shared between sources, which limits filtering by kind: "SlicingError" is used for slice failures and for canvas errors such as toolpath out of bounds, and "PlaterError" for an object over the plate edge and at least one other producer in `Plater.cpp` (around the call to `push_plater_error_notification` near the mesh-combining code). Identity must never be derived from message text.

## Problem 4: the new readers were never triggered at runtime

The readers added for the plate checks and post-slice checks compile and were reviewed against OrcaSlicer's code, but none of their conditions was reproduced, because the harness's test printer has one nozzle and no TPU. Unverified today: two or more TPU filaments, filament not printable, PLA mixed with PETG, nozzle and filament incompatible, filament mixture incompatible, prime tower outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach (left/right nozzle), toolpath outside the plate, toolpath above the print height, nozzle printable-area and printable-height errors after slicing, and filament not printable on the plate surface. Also never reproduced: a slicing failure that names its object, and G-code processor warnings.

Deliver: for each, a reproduction recipe in the real app (which printer profile, filaments, model, and steps), and where feasible a new step in `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` that produces it through native paths and checks the monitor reports it with the right severity and target. A dual-nozzle Bambu profile (H2D) and multi-filament setups are likely needed; `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` describes the in-process fake Bambu printer. For any reader whose text the fork composes from OrcaSlicer's translation strings (the nozzle range and height sentences in `PrintIssueMonitor::collect_result`), compare the result with what OrcaSlicer's own notice says in the stock presentation and report differences. Mark anything you cannot reproduce as unverified; do not fill gaps with plausible explanations.

## Ground rules (Kenneth's)

- Never apply a fix for something you have not reproduced. Search and verify before asserting; label inference as inference.
- Test end to end in the local dev environment. The harness needs a scratch `HOME`; never drive or kill another JusPrin instance on the machine. Build recipe and traps are in the saved notes for this project (worktree build, llvm-ar for the 4 GiB archive, absolute build paths).
- Keep temporary reports untracked and visible; do not commit them.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks.

Hand back one short report: per problem, the recommendation, the evidence, the upstream footprint with merge-simulation results where an upstream edit is proposed, and the decisions Kenneth has to make.

content.text:
The change is made and tested: the upstream footprint is now two added lines in one file, with no new flag. I also added the no-agent dialog and created the task chip. The app in front of you now runs with no agent configured, so you can try the dialog.

## Hiding notices with the existing flag

The header setter, getter and member are gone, and so is the shell's save-and-restore code. The whole upstream edit is:

```cpp
	sort_notifications();
	if (wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden())
		return;
```

**One deviation from the snippet you pasted.** The snippet asked the canvas being drawn (`canvas.legacy_overlays_hidden()`). I built and tested that first, and it failed your rule that notices never show inside the shell: the Check print window is a second canvas that never gets the flag, and it drew OrcaSlicer's notices again. Setting the flag on that canvas would also strip Check print's own stock controls. So the line asks the Prepare canvas instead, which answers "is the shell on" for every canvas. It is still two lines, and Check print now draws no notices.

Switching to classic mode restores the flag, so notices come back there with no extra code. I did not touch the standalone G-code viewer mode; the shell is never installed there, so its notices still show.

Merge simulation against current upstream: no new conflict, and upstream's newer line at the top of that function still runs first.

## No agent configured

Pressing either button now sends nothing to the chat and shows this dialog:

> **Set up the AI assistant**
> The AI assistant isn't set up yet. Set it up in the chat panel, and it can explain this issue and help you fix it.
> [Set up now] [Not now]

"Set up now" opens the chat panel on its setup screen. Tell me if you want different wording.

## Test results on the final code

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Real-app print-issues scenario, light and dark | 42 steps, 354 checks each, 0 failures |
| Notices drawn in Prepare and in Check print | 0 and 0, while OrcaSlicer still holds them underneath |
| Existing shell regression | 529 checks, 0 failures |
| Switch to classic mode | 31 checks, 0 failures |

## Task chip

"Close the gaps left by hiding OrcaSlicer's notices" is waiting for you to start. It covers the four items you quoted: operation notices with no replacement, the flushing-volume warning, future upstream warning kinds, and the readers never triggered at runtime. The handoff tells that agent not to work in this session's worktree, since the feature is still uncommitted here.

## Your question: repeat presses and other plates

Those are two separate open decisions, not one.

- **Repeat presses.** You press "Ask AI" on an issue, get an answer, and press "Ask AI" on the same issue again while nothing about the project has changed. Today the second press does nothing, because it is treated as the same question (the first answer is still in the chat). The alternative is to send the question again each time.
- **Other plates.** OrcaSlicer only checks the plate you are looking at. So the status shows problems for the active plate only; a problem on plate 2 is not shown until you switch to plate 2. The alternative is to mark the other plates as "not checked" somewhere, so "no print issues" is not read as covering the whole project.

Nothing is committed yet.

content.text:
The dialog is now OrcaSlicer's own styled message dialog, and the app in front of you is rebuilt with it (still with no agent configured, so pressing either button shows it). I could not capture a picture of the new dialog from this session, so I have not seen it myself; please check it looks right.

## The dialog

No, what you saw was not OrcaSlicer's default. It was the macOS system alert, which is what you get from the plain wxWidgets message call I used. OrcaSlicer has its own dialog class (`MessageDialog`) for every question it asks, and I should have used that. I have switched to it, with the same wording and the same two buttons ("Set up now", "Not now").

Two side notes:
- The blank square icon in your screenshot came from the test app, which has no icon. The real JusPrin app would have shown its own icon there.
- The fork's other confirmations (14 call sites, for example "Previously opened file") also use the system alert. I left those alone; say if you want them moved to OrcaSlicer's dialog too.

The full scenario passes with the new dialog: 42 steps, 357 checks, 0 failures. The test now presses the real buttons and answers the real dialog, so I removed the stand-in I had added for testing the system alert.

## Repeat presses

No tracking, so I kept it. The message already needs an ID. I build that ID from the issue, which button was pressed, the project's current state, and the chat. The chat's existing duplicate check does the rest. That is about four lines and no stored state.

In practice: pressing the same button again with nothing changed reopens the chat panel, where the earlier answer is, and sends nothing. After any edit, or in a new chat, the same press sends a fresh question.

## Plates

Left as it is: the status shows the active plate only.

Nothing is committed yet. The task you started for the four gaps is running in its own session.

git add -A -- agent-docs resources src tests && git status --short | cat && cat > /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-wonderful-roentgen-83d009/e810f2ea-fa11-42bd-a424-2ee68a666289/scratchpad/commit-msg.txt <<'EOF'
Keep print issues on the Prepare canvas, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI

A print problem was only visible as an OrcaSlicer notice in the corner of
the 3D view, or somewhere back in the chat. Inside the JusPrin shell those
notices are now replaced by a status in the canvas's lower right corner, the
list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about.
The bubble's two buttons send the issue to the project chat.

The list (PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor) holds no rule about what a problem
is. It asks OrcaSlicer's own checks again and reads the state OrcaSlicer
already stores: Print::validate, a copy over the plate's edge, the plate's
filament and nozzle checks, slicing step warnings, the slice result, and why
the last slice failed. An issue exists while its native source reports it.
While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to the print, the
issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and the buttons
are off, so "no print issues" is never shown before a check. Only the
active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer checks.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list or the tool strip. It docks beside the status for a
plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Every finding on one object
shares the bubble through a pager. Selecting an issue selects its copy by
OrcaSlicer's own id, so two objects with one name cannot be confused.

Chat (AgentHost::submit_issue_message, PrintIssues/IssueContext): a press
becomes an ordinary user message, the request sentence with OrcaSlicer's
words quoted beneath it, and carries the issue, its target and the
freshness of the evidence as data for the model. It shares the page's own
message path, obeys the same refusals, and leaves the composer's draft
alone. The issue is looked up again at the press, so one that has cleared
or gone stale is not sent. Ask AI may only read: the turn is offered the
read-only tools and the host refuses a call to any other. Resolve with AI
is an ordinary turn. With no assistant set up, a press sends nothing and
offers to open the chat panel's setup.

OrcaSlicer-owned files: two added lines in
NotificationManager::render_notifications return early while the Prepare
canvas has its legacy overlays hidden, the flag the shell already sets on
install and restores when switching to the classic presentation. Only the
drawing stops; notices are still pushed, timed out and closed. The Prepare
canvas is asked, not the canvas being drawn, because Check print is a
second canvas without the flag and drew the notices again. The reason a
slice failed is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, which Plater.cpp defines
and no header declared; it is declared in a fork header Plater.cpp already
includes, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

Rebase evidence (fork base 3ffb9585d2, upstream/main b3490a1cdc): the
conflict list from git merge-tree is the same with and without this change.
The two lines sit after sort_notifications() because upstream has since
added a line at the top of that function, which they would otherwise have
collided with. No upstream line is deleted or rewritten.

Known limits, recorded in agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md: notices that
are not print problems (export finished, upload and download progress,
update and network notices) have no JusPrin surface yet and are no longer
seen; the "flushing volume set to 0" warning is not read, because its check
is private to GLCanvas3D; a warning kind upstream adds later needs a reader
before it is shown. The plate-check and post-slice readers were not
triggered at runtime: the test printer has one nozzle and no TPU.

Tests: tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp covers placement and the chat
message; tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp covers the message path, the
read-only limit and its refusal; the token guards cover the two new widths.
The shell harness gains --print-issues, which drives the real app through
42 steps (validation, placement, slicing warnings and failures, camera and
object moves, both buttons, stale and cleared issues, deletion, undo, plate
switch, project replacement, Check print) in light and dark, and
--manual-print-issues for hands-on use.
EOF

The feature is committed and now on `jusprin-newui` in the main checkout as commit `6394191523`. I have not pushed it.

## What happened

1. **Committed** on this session's branch as `b1dccfb461`. The temporary report and its screenshots folder stayed untracked.
2. **Base had diverged.** `jusprin-newui` had three commits my base did not have, and my base commit itself had been rewritten there under a different ID. Ten of the files I changed were also changed on `jusprin-newui`.
3. **Tested before landing.** I replayed the commit on top of the current `jusprin-newui` in my own worktree first. It applied without conflicts, and I then built and tested that exact result.
4. **Cherry-picked** the tested commit onto `jusprin-newui` in the main checkout. The main checkout had no tracked changes at the time, and the resulting tree is identical to the one I tested.

## Test results on top of current `jusprin-newui`

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Print-issues scenario in the real app, light and dark | 42 steps, 357 checks each, 0 failures |
| Existing shell regression | 526 checks, 0 failures |
| Switch to classic mode | 31 checks, 0 failures |
| Chat host unit tests | 4,749 assertions pass |
| Layout and message unit tests | 584 assertions pass |
| Theme tests | 135 assertions pass |
| Token guard tests | pass, apart from the one failure the suite already marks as allowed |

## Things to know

- **The main checkout's own build is now stale.** I did not build there; it will need a rebuild to pick up the commit.
- **I closed the hands-on test app** before rebuilding. Say if you want it reopened.
- **Two leftover branches** in my worktree are now redundant: `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1` (the commit on the old base) and `claude/print-issues-on-newui` (the tested copy). I left both in place.
- **The background task you started** for the four gaps was told the feature is uncommitted in this worktree. It can now branch from `jusprin-newui` instead.
- **The dialog's look is still unchecked by me.** I could not capture a picture of the restyled "Set up the AI assistant" dialog from this session.
